per_claim.note: Replication retrieved and analyzed 68/77 assemblies from PRJNA480281; 9/77 were unavailable as GenBank assemblies at query time, so the full stated isolate set could not be fully reconstituted.

In-silico serovar calling was concordant for 67/68, with the remaining case effectively concordant at the antigenic-formula level (Reading). Dominant serovars reported by the paper are consistent with the replication’s SeqSero2 results.

Paper reports phenotypic resistance/decreased-susceptibility rates; replication computed genotypic acquired-class prevalence. Some directions align (e.g., no ESBL/cephalosporin genes detected; substantial quinolone-associated genes), but several class prevalences are notably lower genotypically than the paper’s phenotypes (e.g., tetracycline 33.8% vs 40.3%; beta-lactam 11.8% vs 20–26%; phenicol 10.3% vs 19.5%), and ciprofloxacin decreased-susceptibility (>55%) is not directly reproduced by PMQR gene prevalence (47.1%).
MDR prevalence was close: 23.5% (16/68) vs paper 26% (basis: ≥3 classes). Difference is plausibly attributable to missing 9 isolates and genotype-vs-phenotype/definition implementation details.

Directionally, ground beef had higher MDR (33.3% vs 18.2%), but the association was not statistically significant in the replication (chi2=1.98, p=0.159) versus the paper’s strong significance (chi2=12.0, p=0.0005). This is a substantive mismatch, potentially driven by the missing 9 isolates and/or phenotype-vs-genotype MDR classification.

Typhimurium comprised 37.5% of MDR isolates (6/16) vs paper’s 40%, consistent in magnitude. However, the replication did not reproduce the reported strong overall serovar–MDR association statistic (chi2=24.5, p<0.0001), and with only 7 Typhimurium total, power/coverage differences may matter.

Replication found 6 Typhimurium with the full SGI1 penta-resistance gene set (aadA2, blaCARB-2, floR, sul1, tetG), matching the paper’s described cassette content; the paper’s count (9/10 Typhimurium) cannot be fully checked because only 7 Typhimurium were present in the 68 analyzed assemblies.

Replication detected 0 QRDR/soxRS mutations and 0 ramR mutations using AMRFinderPlus’s curated mutation reporting, conflicting with the paper’s claim of 100% QRDR/soxRS mutations and a strong ramR–MDR association. This may reflect a methods/catalog difference (custom mutation calling in the paper vs AMRFinder’s mutation set), but as tested here the claim does not reproduce.

justification: Core genomic findings around serovar calling, overall MDR prevalence, and the SGI1 penta-resistance gene set in Typhimurium are broadly reproduced on real isolate genomes, albeit with incomplete isolate coverage (68/77). However, the paper’s key inferential claim about MDR being significantly higher in ground beef is not reproduced, and the point-mutation claims are contradicted under the replication’s mutation-calling approach. Several resistance-class prevalences also diverge, consistent with phenotype-vs-genotype measurement differences.
